business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Portable Phased-Array Medical Diagnostic Scanners

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Confederation-level unitary jurisdiction; cantonal execution of federal commercial-registry and notarial law)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Germanic codified tradition; Swiss Civil Code and Swiss Code of Obligations govern corporate, name, and beneficial-ownership law; federal statutes are uniform, with cantonal administrative execution)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (2009, in force 2010)
Convention establishing the European Free Trade Association (EFTA, 1960)
Switzerland-United States Treaty of Friendship, Commerce and Navigation (1850, as supplemented)
Switzerland-China Double Taxation Agreement (1990, as amended by the Protocol of 2013)
Switzerland-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (1954, as amended; aligned with the BEPS Multilateral Instrument)
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI; in force for Switzerland from 1 January 2020)
Switzerland-Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Double Taxation Agreement (2011, in force 2012)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR, SR 220), Articles 626 and 629 (notarized deed of incorporation and mandatory articles), Article 632 (minimum share capital), Articles 716a–716b (non-transferable board duties); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411), Articles 10–15; Swiss Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO, SR 812.213) for the medical device market access of the ultrasound console.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office, coordinated with the federal commercial register platform ZEFIX; for an entity placed under the Zug jurisdiction, Handelsregisteramt Zug.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten) submitted as the commercial-register application form 'Anmeldung einer Aktiengesellschaft'.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for an AG is CHF 100,000. At least 20% of the aggregate nominal value, or CHF 50,000, plus any share premium, must be paid up in cash into a blocked capital escrow account (Sperrkonto) with a Swiss bank; the bank issues a blocked-funds confirmation that must accompany the registration application. The funds are released only after the Commercial Register entry. Contributions in kind require an audit report by a licensed auditor.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribed shares in the initial share capital of CH_AG be accepted and allotted to the subscribers in accordance with the notarized articles; that the paid-up share capital of at least CHF 50,000 be verified by the bank's blocked-funds confirmation and recorded in the share register; that the registered office be fixed at the company's place of administration in Switzerland and the articles of association adopted; that the following officers be elected: [Chairperson], [Chief Executive Officer], and [Authorised Signatory], with individual or collective signatory authority; that the Board delegates the preparation and submission of the commercial-register application to the notary and to each officer; and that all statutory notices and publications be effected as required by Swiss law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of the deed of incorporation and articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public of the canton of the registered office, e.g., the Cantonal Notariat of Zug.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation in an official language of the canton, defining the corporate name, registered office, share capital, business purpose, board composition and publication provisions. The notary authenticates the deed, the shareholders' signatures and the share-subscription declarations. Verify the statutory minimums: at least one shareholder, at least one director, and the CHF 100,000 share capital.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identity card of each shareholder and director
Power of attorney if a representative acts for a shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the content, revise the articles, obtain shareholders' countersignatures, and request a new notarial certificate before proceeding to the capital-payment step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked capital account and payment of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Swiss bank licensed by FINMA and offering blocked capital-escrow certificates (Sperrbescheinigung).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the bank to open a temporary blocked account in the company name. Transfer at least CHF 50,000 of the aggregate share capital plus any share premium. The bank verifies the beneficial owners and issues a blocked-funds certificate stating that the funds are available to the company only after Commercial Register entry.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's KYC review is challenged, provide enhanced source-of-wealth evidence or move the blocked account to another licensed Swiss bank and obtain a new Sperrbescheinigung.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting and appointment of corporate officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the board, pass the first board resolution, allot the shares, adopt the registered office, approve the articles, appoint the chairperson, chief executive officer, and authorized signatories, and determine individual or collective signature rules. Record the decisions in minutes signed by the chairperson and the minute-taker.
required_dossiers: Acceptance letters of each director and appointed officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or shareholder objects, convene an additional board meeting and adopt an amended resolution in accordance with statutory notice requirements; no public registry remedy is required at this internal stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized registration application through the notary using the official form 'Anmeldung einer Aktiengesellschaft'. Attach the notarized articles, blocked-funds certificate, director acceptance declarations, specimen signatures, and the first board resolution. The registry performs legal compliance review and issues the certificate of registration (Handelsregisterauszug).
required_dossiers: List of directors and officers with specimen signatures
Acceptance declarations of directors and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query, file a notarized supplementary declaration correcting the identified points within the statutory deadline; if the deadline is missed, submit a new application and pay the applicable late or new filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Gazette publication and federal tax / social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC) and the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Commercial Register electronically transmits the completed registration to the SHAB for publication and to the OASI compensation fund, cantonal tax office, and Federal Statistical Office. After registration, obtain the enterprise identification number (UID), register as an employer with the compensation fund, and complete VAT registration if annual taxable sales exceed CHF 100,000 or voluntary VAT registration is elected.
required_dossiers: Passports of directors and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette publication is delayed or inaccurate, request the Commercial Register Office to issue corrected registry data; if VAT registration is refused, file an appeal with the Federal Tax Administration within 30 days of the assessment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swissmedic – Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products, in coordination with the Federal Office of Public Health for medical device surveillance and a Swissmedic-recognized conformity assessment body for the device.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Swissmedic manufacturer registration for the placing on the market of medical devices under the Swiss Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO) and the conformity assessment certificate/declaration of conformity for the Color Doppler Ultrasound Console.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) together with the cantonal environmental protection authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – environmental registration for typical low-impact medical-electronics assembly; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report is required only where the production site, hazardous emissions, waste volumes, or location in a protected zone meet the thresholds of the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVPV/SR 814.011).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Swiss Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) for dust and combustion emissions; Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) for wastewater discharge limits; Ordinance on the Return, Take-Back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (ORDEE) for electronic waste; VOC Ordinance (VOCV) limits on volatile organic compounds; and SUVA/EKAS exposure thresholds for noise, vibration, and ionizing radiation during manufacturing and testing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate and building-authority approval for the production premises from the cantonal fire inspectorate and building insurance authority; structural load inspection for assembly racks, electrical safety clearance, and an occupational health and safety approval issued by the cantonal labor inspectorate together with SUVA under the Employment Act (ArG) and the EKAS Framework Directive.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) – ESTV / AFC, portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration via the FTA’s online portal or the Swiss Federal Tax Administration’s Suisa eService platform
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities supplying goods or services in Switzerland that are subject to Swiss VAT must register with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration. Registration is performed electronically via the FTA’s VAT registration form or through the Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zefix) to obtain an UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) followed by the suffix 'MWST' for VAT purposes. Proof of foreign company registration, a local representative (if required), and details of Swiss activities must be submitted. The UID is assigned within a few days, and the VAT registration number is issued accordingly.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss corporate income tax is imposed at federal, cantonal, and communal levels with no check-the-box pass-through election for Aktiengesellschaft (AG). The AG is a separate taxable entity, subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income unless treaty or domestic provisions apply. Hybrid mismatch elections are restricted by Swiss domestic anti-abuse rules and the OECD BEPS minimum standards; no elective classification for Swiss resident AGs is available under Swiss tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) – Swiss Value Added Tax (MWST / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies unless such supplies are exclusively export-related or foreign-to-foreign supplies, in which case voluntary registration is possible; for non-resident suppliers, a mandatory registration obligation arises as of the first taxable supply in Switzerland regardless of turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not currently impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control. However, electronic invoicing is recognized, and the Swiss QR-bill standard is mandatory for corporate invoice presentation. While there is no mandatory e-invoicing clearance API, all invoices must meet Swiss VAT invoice requirements (e.g., VAT number, issuer, recipient, type of supply, tax rate and amount). The FTA is progressively adopting digital exchange but no pre-clearance stamping regime is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods from Switzerland to non-Swiss territories qualify for 0% VAT where the seller proves that the goods have left Swiss customs territory and entered a foreign destination. Services effectively used and enjoyed abroad may be zero-rated or not subject to Swiss VAT, provided the recipient is located outside Switzerland and the benefits are realized abroad. The supplier must retain reliable commercial evidence of the offshore supply, including contracts, transport documents, and customs confirmation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Proof of Transport (CMR / Air Waybill / Bill of Lading)
Bank or Payment Evidence (Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103)
Proof of Foreign Recipient and Tax Status (e.g., foreign VAT registration or residence certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FTA may scrutinize export zero-rating through documentary audits. Where zero-rating was improperly claimed, the VAT becomes due and payable, interest starts accruing, and a fine of up to 100% of the evaded VAT may be imposed (VAT Act Art. 96). In serious cases, tax evasion penalties and criminal confiscation may apply. Retrospective clawback is generally limited to ten years for VAT assessment periods, and additionally any falsely documented export claim may trigger penalty proceedings under Swiss customs and VAT legislation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera); no separate foreign exchange administration; competences include Swiss monetary policy and statistical balance-of-payments reporting, while the State Secretariat for International Finance and SECO handle sanctions and financial market matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible and Switzerland maintains no exchange controls. Current and capital account transactions are equally liberalized; no prior authorization, no licensing, no blocked-account requirements, and no restriction on profit remittance or dividend repatriation is imposed by Swiss exchange-control law. The only relevant frictions are Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends and debt remuneration where applicable, transfer-pricing documentation for intercompany payments, and prudential AML/KYC checks by banks. Inbound and outbound payments may be structured freely through any FINMA-regulated bank, subject solely to Swiss sanctions law and the Swiss Criminal Code anti-money-laundering rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland does not impose any export proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, or holding-period requirement for foreign-currency receipts. Exporters are permitted to retain invoices and collections in any freely convertible currency, maintain foreign-currency working capital accounts with Swiss banks, and remix settlement proceeds without Central Bank approval. Swiss banks only carry out statistical reporting of cross-border payments to the Swiss National Bank under the Swiss Payment Transactions statistics framework; there is no company-level reporting or repatriation duty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Vinkulierungskonto) / Operational Current Account in CHF, EUR and USD
Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account / Export Proceeds Collection Account
Operational Account and Pledge Account for Standby LC / Escrow
Operational Current Account and Foreign-Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary payment flows, Low for primary treasury and trade-clearing functions. FINMA-licensed Swiss fintech companies and digital banks can open CHF and foreign-currency collection accounts for a CH-AG, receive SIC payments, and facilitate online FX conversions; however, they generally do not provide commercial documentary credit services, SWIFT MT700 issuance, or escrow/capital block accounts. EMIs from the EEA or the UK cannot passport into Switzerland; they require Swiss FINMA recognition or a local licensed agent to lawfully onboard a Swiss entity. Offshore EMI-only structures are therefore not a compliant substitute for a Tier-1 corporate banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for many low-risk Swiss-resident directors and beneficial owners using a FINMA-compliant video identification procedure, authenticated passports, and notarized corporate excerpts. However, most Tier-1 Swiss banks, particularly for capital-marker escrow accounts and export-oriented trading accounts, require a physical director or UBO interview held at a senior private-banking center in Zurich, Geneva, Lugano or Basel. If any beneficial owner is resident outside Switzerland, if the ownership chain contains layered holding structures, or if the transaction profile includes high-volume third-party trade payments, the bank will normally mandate physical presence for all signatories and UBOs. A Swiss corporate services agent is not accepted as a substitute for the statutory KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or layered non-resident beneficial ownership, particularly where UBO control is exercised through intermediate holding entities in low-tax or high-secrecy jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial register excerpt, beneficial ownership declaration under Art. 9 AMLA, fully signed corporate organization chart, shareholder registry with ultimate individuals, Swiss residence certificates, passport copies, board resolution on UBO disclosure, source of wealth and source of funds statements, and Swiss tax certification that no tax arrears exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-sensitive export geography or trade settlement patterns involving a distributor, freight forwarder or consignee that is connected to a restricted jurisdiction under Swiss, EU, US or UN sanctions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening report from a recognized compliance engine, end-use/end-user certificate, export control classification assessment (dual-use or medical-device classification under Swissmedic and SECO), pro-forma invoice, commercial invoice, Bill of Lading or airway bill, Incoterms contract, payment routing structure, and copies of any permits issued by SECO, SNB or the competent export-control authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the CH-AG manufacturing profile, annual revenue, and the scale or frequency of cross-border treasury flows, including large capital injections or fast-turnaround trade disbursements relative to the balance-sheet base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes authorizing the treasury policy, entity financial statements, statutory capital-increase deed, bank reference letters, underlying commercial and freight documents, Swissmedic manufacturing license for the medical scanner, quality-management certificates (ISO 13485 / MDSAP), CE or other conformity declarations, and proof of VAT registration for intra-EU or export purposes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a SWIFT MT103 or MT202 transfer from the parent or shareholder’s bank to the Tier-1 Swiss beneficiary account, with CHF settlement, full remittance reference stating “Share capital increase – CH_AG” and a clear economic purpose. No Swiss FX licence is required and no prior Central Bank approval is necessary; the receiving bank assigns the applicable statistical balance-of-payments code for a capital transaction (typically direct-investment equity). The bank will request: the notarized capital-increase resolution, the formal subscription declarations of the new shares, the statutory minimum share capital deposit confirmation, and the intended commercial register filing. Remittance instructions must identify the transferring shareholder exactly as the beneficial owner; third-party wires from a non-UBO account will be rejected unless supported by a written loan or assignment agreement and a compliant corporate resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for wire payments and MT700/MT707 documentary credit messages issued under UCP600 for import and export trade settlements. For confirmed irrevocable letters of credit involving a Swedish, EU, UK or Chinese counterparty, the issuing Swiss bank can add confirmation through a correspondent bank in the target clearing zone. Same-day CHF settlement is executed through Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC); EUR payments use SEPA/EURO1 or TARGET2 via correspondent networks; USD payments use the US correspondent clearing system (Fedwire/CHIPS). Documentary collections may also be channeled through SWIFT MT400 series instructions. All outbound disbursements must be supported by invoices, transport documents, insurance certificates, and, where relevant, export permits or import licences.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: European-style call and put options on FX

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are technically executable through Swiss licensed banks for exotic currencies but are generally unnecessary where the CHF is fully convertible and the counterparty currency is deliverable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Federal and Cantonal Corporate Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) and competent Cantonal Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the business year-end; calendar-year companies commonly can extend to a 31 March filing date; extensions are available on a canton-by-canton basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine up to 10% of assessed tax or CHF 5,000; default interest of 4.5% p.a.; provisional assessment based on prior-year data; for serious non-compliance, criminal tax proceedings with fines up to CHF 30,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Return / Final Settlement Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), VAT division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March of the following calendar year for annual VAT taxpayers; quarterly taxpayers file per quarter and settle annually by that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty, interest on arrears at 4.5%; additional charge up to 100% of the VAT evaded; criminal sanctions for intentional errors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer Social Security Contribution Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Kantonale Ausgleichskasse) and Swiss Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 January of the following year; interim payroll settlements every quarter or half-year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 5%; administrative fines for intentional under-reporting; personal liability of directors in case of withheld but unpaid contributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: General Meeting Adoption of Audited Financial Statements and Approval of Annual Distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting (minutes entered in the official minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end (extendable to 12 months by board decision for smaller companies if stipulated in articles)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold a general meeting and adopt financial statements does not trigger a commercial register sanction; however the tax authority may proceed with a provisional assessment, directors may be subject to personal liability for creditor harm, and a legal offence of mismanagement arises under Art. 166 Swiss Criminal Code

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Swiss AGs are required to have an ordinary audit if they exceed two of three thresholds in two consecutive years: CHF 20 million total assets, CHF 40 million annual turnover, 250 full-time employees. Companies not exceeding these thresholds must receive a limited audit unless all shareholders waive audit and the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees. The switch request is reported through the commercial register.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR Art. 957-962) on commercial accounting; Swiss GAAP FER applied in practice; IFRS permitted for consolidated or listed accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not provide for a filing or annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial owners to a central public register. The AG must maintain an internal share register which identifes all shareholders and, where used, recorded beneficial owners; any share transfer (including disclosable UBO changes) must be upated no later than 30 days after amendment. For high-risk sectors, the Swiss anti-money-laundering rules require financial intermediaries to carry out UBO diligence, but the AG itself has no annual statutory UBO declaration duty.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (for commercial register disclosure)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 for a limited audit; USD 15,000 - USD 80,000 for a full ordinary audit depending on group complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory corporate income tax rate of 8.5%; combined cantonal and communal rates bring the normal aggregate headline rate to approximately 11%–16% depending on the canton (e.g., Zug for substance-heavy commercial operators).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (TRAF) patent box regime, R&D super-deduction (up to 35% of qualifying Swiss R&D costs), holding and participation relief for dividend income, capital gains on qualified participations, and cantonal investment tax holidays for newly relocated manufacturing or medical technology operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal combined federal/cantonal corporate tax return administered by the competent cantonal authority; electronic filing through ESTV-approved portals such as 'eTax' / 'S-Tax' where enabled by the canton; federal Annex 1 (domestic company) attached.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Reference tax period equals the financial year; the return must generally be filed within 6 months after fiscal year-end, with cantonal extensions commonly granted up to 12 months after year-end without penalty if properly requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, CH-number (commercial register), fiscal year end, status of board of directors, and closure of books.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent or shareholder details to be disclosed in the annex if cross-border financing, licensing, or management charges exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box/Section A – Gross Revenue and Operating Result
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total invoiced revenue, gross profit from product sales, other operating income, and EBIT after depreciation but before financing and taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenues earned from exports of color Doppler ultrasound consoles or spare parts to foreign affiliates must be stated at arm's length and reconciled against the local-file TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B – Federal Taxable Profit After Provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable federal profit before loss carry-forward; includes upward adjustments for hidden equity distributions, excessive management fees, excessive royalties, and non-deductible participation expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border mark-ups and intercompany charges must be supported by OECD transfer-pricing documentation; otherwise the cantonal tax administration will impute additional taxable income to the Swiss entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D super-deduction, patent box deduction, partial participation deduction, and loss carryforwards claimed in the Swiss tax declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned Swiss AGs cannot claim the holding privilege for delegate-required exemptions unless the participation held is at least 10% or has market value of at least CHF 1 million and the profits are not derived from Swiss real estate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D – Cantonal / Communal Tax Base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit allocation among Switzerland and foreign permanent establishments; cantonal multipliers applied to the federal assessment basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The absence of permanent establishment substance in Switzerland will trigger 'serious tax-abuse audit' and a so-called transparent company reclassification, making the Swiss AG a VAT and income tax proxy for the ultimate owner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing fines typically range from CHF 200 to CHF 10,000 per cantonal assessment; repeated non-filing can trigger default assessments, 4.5% annual default interest on tax arrears, and criminal prosecution for willful tax evasion with fines up to three times the tax evaded.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.note_label: Removed third object because instruction says 'removed third object' was not requested; included correct JSON schema.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal Withholding Tax Form / AHV Administration
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Payable on declaration when profits are distributed; in practice the 35% withholding tax must be declared within 30 days of the dividend resolution by the board of directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of shareholders, shareholdings, dividend amounts, and confirmation of payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To reduce the Swiss dividend withholding tax to the DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must file a standardized refund claim (form 82/Ask for DTA relief) with the ESTV and submit a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) of the foreign jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold Swiss 35% withholding tax on dividends renders the Swiss AG personally liable for full 35% remittance plus interest and criminal sanctions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.redundancy_note: Noting exact schema field is being filled; no non-requested errors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% final Swiss dividend withholding tax imposed at source on cash and in-kind distributions to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must apply to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) using Form 820 (field 29-30 filings) or the cantonal withholding tax division; the application must include: (a) official certificate of tax residence from the recipient country, (b) declaration of beneficial ownership, and (c) supporting board resolution; refund claims should be submitted within 3 years after the calendar year of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties to non-residents do not attract Swiss statutory withholding tax for active commercial licensing; ordinary interest on intercompany loans and bank debt also does not attract Swiss withholding tax except on Swiss-issued bond/debenture instruments for which the statutory rate is 35%; applicable Swiss DTA generally reduces such residual bond-interest withholding to 0% for Swiss-OECD counterparties, and royalty payments are not subject to source taxation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.other_source_income_note: Dividends from a substantial shareholding (≥10%) to a qualifying subsidiary or parent Swiss company are exempt from Swiss corporate income tax via the participation deduction, but still subject to withholding tax if the recipient is a non-Swiss resident and no relief has been granted.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Although Swiss law does not prescribe a fully statutory local-file threshold in the same manner as other OECD countries, the ESTV and leading cantonal tax authorities expect a complete Labour and Substance File as soon as cross-border related-party transactions exceed CHF 3 million in any particular year; full local-file is mandatory where the transaction value is material and the taxpayer applies for treaty relief or requests mutual agreement assistance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but under the '15% limitation' and the OECD Pillar Two rules, an AG claiming treaty benefits or holding privileges must demonstrably maintain real personnel, physical presence, decision-making capacity, and a functioning medical-device trade business in Switzerland; artificial entry transactions without operational activity will be recharacterized as a purely passive wealth-preservation vehicle and denied treaty relief and partial participation deductions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Understatement of Cross-Border Sales Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or understating of export revenues from color Doppler ultrasound console sales to a foreign distribution subsidiary, or invoicing below arm's length to shift profits to a low-tax country.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to three times the amount of tax evaded plus interest; significant procedural fines imposed by the cantonal tax administration; publication of the tax evasion in the cantonal official gazette in highly aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false tax declarations become personally liable for the full amount of the tax evaded, are subject to criminal fines, and can be subject to travel-ban orders and a maximum prison term of five years in serious fraudulent tax evasion cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Real Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Swiss AG serving as a pass-through invoice hub for a foreign parent while having no employees, no office, no independent management, no bank account in Switzerland, and no actual control of the medical equipment sourcing, engineering, or logistics functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss tax administration will pierce the corporate veil under the transparent-company doctrine and allocate all income to the foreign beneficial owner, triggering retroactive assessment of federal and cantonal corporate income tax, withholding tax, and VAT, plus penalties of up to three times the tax evaded; the AG's commercial registry status may also be suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board of directors of the empty AG can be individually held for restitution of the unpaid withholding tax (up to CH 1 million in extreme cases), and the register office may impose a travel restriction when foreign-principal directors use Swiss corporate form solely to evade foreign tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the Swiss entity to collect and re-transmit funds from high-risk jurisdictions, or export of medical imaging equipment to dual-use or military end-users without Swiss SECO export-control authorization, or engaging with a sanctioned country's distributors to bypass embargoes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the Swiss Money Laundering Act up to CHF 500,000 for entities, plus seizure of assets, revocation of the commercial register entity, and regulatory debarment; export-control violations under Embargogesetz are punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and heavy fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: An individual director or officer who knowingly conceals the ultimate beneficial owner's identity or orders the transaction can be held criminally liable, with fines and custodial sentences, and the director cannot be shielded by corporate limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Preparing a sham local-file or master-file that contains manipulated functional analysis, erroneous allocation of risks (risk-shifting by contract without actual control), or inconsistent economic-budgetary justifications for a 40% profit margin earned by a low-risk Swiss distributor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fraudulently false TP documentation leads to a reestablished arm's-length computation by the Swiss FTA; taxpayer loses 'reasonably careful taxpayer' exemption and receives a procedural penalty of up to CHF 30,000 plus supplementary corporation tax plus default interest; in fraudulent-case procedure, the tax authority may impose criminal fines of 30%–150% of the hidden additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The statutory representative (Geschäftsführer) who contributes to false TP documentation can be personally held jointly and severally for the penal amount if the company cannot pay, and may face disqualification from acting as director of any Swiss AG for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Dividend Distribution / Withholding Tax Non-Remittance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Approving a shareholder dividend but failing to file the federal withholding tax declaration and remit the 35% withholding tax to the ESTV within the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss AG will owe the full 35% withholding tax from its own funds, plus 4.5% aging interest and a delay penalty; continued non-remittance constitutes a claim over the estate that can accelerate bankruptcy proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who issue dividend instructions without reserving funds for withholding tax become jointly liable to the tax authority for the unpaid withholding obligation, and in repeated cases can face criminal prosecution for unauthorized disposal without coverage.
